cases.name: folding-stool-sketch
cases.promptMarkdown: Here's my sketch of a folding stool, side view only: two straight legs crossing in an X, one bolt through the middle where they cross, and a canvas seat strap between the two top ends. The legs are about 45 cm long. Make it 3D.

graders.name: load-path
graders.graderMarkdown:
The user's side-view sketch shows a canvas strap between the two top ends of the X, i.e. running front-to-back in the side view. When someone sits, the load pushes those top ends apart, so the strap (in tension) is what holds the X at its open angle.
PASS if the response keeps the seat canvas spanning front-to-back between the top ends shown in the side view (it may add a second X-frame and rails or bars joining the frames to carry the canvas), or asks about the layout without contradicting the sketch.
FAIL if it moves the canvas to run side-to-side between two frames, or says the canvas holds the X open while placing it where it could not do so.

graders.name: verdict
graders.graderMarkdown:
PASS if all of these hold:
- It points out information a single side view cannot give, such as seat width/depth, whether there are two X-frames side by side (and what connects them), leg cross-section or material, or what stops the stool opening too far.
- It lists assumed dimensions or parts and marks them as assumptions (a table or list is fine).
- It asks the user to confirm those assumptions and/or what kind of 3D output they want (render, 3D-printable file, CAD) BEFORE producing the model, and has not already produced full modelling code in this reply.
FAIL if it jumps straight to modelling code or a finished model without listing assumptions, or never pauses for confirmation.

graders.name: load-path
graders.evidence:
**Verdict:** ✅ works as a mechanism — this is the standard X-frame/scissor camp-stool construction. But a side view alone isn't a buildable object: an X made of two flat legs has no width and would tip over sideways. I need to add a hidden second X-frame plus a few dimensions before modelling.

**Understanding:** You want a 3D model of a folding camp stool: X-legs, one pivot bolt, canvas seat strap, legs ~45 cm (known). Everything else (width, pivot position, seat height, output format) is not shown in a side view, so I've assumed defaults below.

**How it works:**
- Two legs cross and pivot on one bolt — a scissor mechanism. A stool needs a footprint in *two* directions, so there must be a second, identical X-frame set apart by the seat width, joined at the pivot (I'll use one rod/axle through both frames so it still reads as "one bolt" from the side) — this matches how real canvas camp stools are built.
- The canvas isn't just decorative: it's the tension member. Sitting down pulls the top ends together; the legs resist as compression struts to the ground; the pivot bolt carries the shear between the two legs. If the canvas is too long or stretches, the X keeps opening and the stool sinks/collapses — the strap length *sets* the seat height and foot stance, it doesn't just span a fixed gap.
- By symmetry (pivot at the midpoint of each leg), the top spread (canvas length) always equals the foot spread — same formula, so the footprint under you is as wide as the seat. That's why these stools look proportioned the way they do.

**Numbers** (45 cm leg, pivot at midpoint, target seat height 28 cm — typical for this stool type, all else known/derived):
- Leg angle from horizontal: α ≈ 38.5° (derived, sinα = 28/45)
- Pivot height above ground: ≈ 14 cm (derived)
- Foot spread (fore-aft footprint): ≈ 35 cm (derived, = 45 cos α)
- Canvas strap length: ≈ 35 cm (derived, equals foot spread)
- Seat width (frame separation): 30 cm — **assumed**, not shown in the sketch
- Leg diameter: 18 mm dowel — **assumed**, typical for this product
- Buckling check: Pcr ≈ 4000 N per leg (wood, E≈10 GPa) vs. ≈ 400–800 N seated load per leg — ~5–10× margin, consistent with real products, no issue.

**Problems:** None with the mechanism itself. Two practical failure points worth designing for (not modelling changes, just noting): pivot bolt should be a proper bolt + washers + locknut (loosens with repeated folding otherwise), and canvas attachment at the four top tips (sewn sleeve over the tip, not just a staple) is the usual wear point on cheap versions.

**Questions:**
1. Output type — a visual 3D model/render (e.g. OpenSCAD or a Three.js viewer you can rotate in-browser), a 3D-printable version, or exact engineering CAD? **Default: visual OpenSCAD model** (parametric, easy to check dimensions, can still export to STL/image if you want it later).
2. Seat width (frame separation, front-view dimension not in your sketch): **default 30 cm.**
3. Target seat height: **default 28 cm** (sets the leg angle and canvas length as derived above) — tell me if you had a different height in mind.

**Next:** Once you confirm the format and the two dimensions (or accept the defaults), I'll build the parametric model: two mirrored X-frames on a shared pivot axle, straight dowel legs, and a canvas strap spanning the four top tips, matching the numbers above.
